summary: Hiralal Rasikdas Kapadia worked in Indology and religious studies. In 1947, he was attested as Professor of Ardhamagadhi at MTB Arts College and as University Teacher for Ph.D. in Ardhamagadhi at the University of Mumbai.

An expert in history, archaeology, and Buddhist and religious studies, Woodward studied at Harvard and Yale. He taught at Silpakorn, Michigan, and Vermont, and served as curator of Asian art at the Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

Hirananda Sastri was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College and Oriental College. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India, held museum curatorial roles, was Government Epigraphist, and directed archaeology for Baroda State (1934–1942).

Hirofumi Isoda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University by 1966. He held posts as lecturer and associate professor at Tohoku University and was an attested professor emeritus at Shimane University.

Hirofumi Toda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a professor at Tokushima University from circa 1980 to 2002 and held an appointment at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

Hiroko Kawanami is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott. Her academic appointments include serving as a senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016).

Hiroko Matsuoka specializes in Indology and philosophy. She earned degrees from Hiroshima University and the University of Leipzig, and held research staff posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2021–2023) and the University of Vienna (2024).

Hiromasa Tosaki specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Kyushu and Harvard under teachers including Shōren Ihara and Daniel H. H. Ingalls, he served as a professor at Kyushu University from circa 1974 to 1993.

Hiromi Habata is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Freiburg. She held posts at the University of Munich, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Hiromi Yoshimura is a scholar in Buddhist studies. His career includes appointments at Ryukoku University, where he is attested as a lecturer in 1987 and affiliated in 2006.
Hiromichi Kato is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Ryogon Fukuhara. His academic appointments include serving as a lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).

Hiromitsu Ikuma is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a doctorate at Tohoku University by 2019. He has served as a researcher at Taisho University and at the Institute of Buzan Sectarian Studies.
Hiromu Kitanishi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Otani University, where he later served as a professor (attested 1980).
Hironari Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies and held a post at Bukkyo University. He was also attested as a lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.

Hironobu Minami specializes in Buddhist studies. His career includes positions as a research assistant at the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015) and associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).
Hiroo Kashiwagi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo circa 1958–1963. He was attested as a professor at Mie Chukyo University in 1982.

Hiroo Sato is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University. He held posts at Morioka College (~1984–1993) and served as a professor at Tohoku University (~2001–2019).

Hiroshi Aoyagi specializes in linguistics, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at International Christian University and the University of Southern California, and became a professor at Nanzan University in 1989.

Hiroshi Araki is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University. He taught at Aichi Prefectural University and Osaka University, and was a professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies from 2010 to 2025.

Hiroshi Arami is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who held lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
